![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The double type assertion `as unknown as CompiledPrompt` is redundant here because `compiledPromptFaultFixture` is already explicitly typed as `unknown` in `fixtures.ts`. You can simplify this to a single assertion: `as CompiledPrompt`.

```suggestion
      scenario === 'sample' ? compiledPromptFixture : (compiledPromptFaultFixture as CompiledPrompt)
```

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve input-dependent prompt output**

For any mock caller that compiles an input other than `promptCompilerInputFixture`, this now returns the fixture prompt and metadata for the glam kitten instead of reflecting the provided description, glam level, density, line thickness, border style, or caption. That makes contract/dev tests using the mock exercise the wrong prompt content and can hide regressions in downstream safety or image-generation flow that depend on the compiled prompt matching the user request.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
